sa_market_summary: The Ford EcoSport was South Africa's third most popular used SUV in 2025, with 4,254 sales at an average of R200,812 and 85,243km according to AutoTrader. Sold locally from 2013 until production ended in 2022, it offered a 1.5 naturally aspirated petrol, a 1.0 EcoBoost turbo petrol and a 1.5 TDCi diesel. It is cheap to buy for a crossover and has good ground clearance for SA roads, but the 1.0 EcoBoost has well-documented cooling system and wet timing belt problems, so service history matters more than mileage.

known_faults.description: The most reported EcoSport fault. Brittle plastic coolant hose connectors, degas bottle and heater hoses crack, and the plastic thermostat housing can warp. The engine loses coolant, sometimes with no visible leak, and overheating can crack or warp the cylinder head. Ford ran a recall for this on some cars.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Check the coolant level when cold and look for white residue around hoses and the expansion tank. Watch the temperature gauge on a long test drive and check for white exhaust smoke or a sweet smell. Ask whether recall work was done.
known_faults.estimated_repair_zar: R3,000 - R8,000 (hoses/housing); R35,000 - R80,000 (head or engine)
known_faults.source: UK used-car guides (Motorloom, ClickMechanic), Ford recall notices

known_faults.description: The 1.0 EcoBoost's timing belt runs in engine oil. Wrong oil or stretched service intervals make the belt shed rubber that can block the oil pickup, starving the engine of oil.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Demand a stamped service history showing Ford-spec oil at the correct intervals. Ask whether the belt has been inspected or replaced and check for a low oil pressure warning.
known_faults.estimated_repair_zar: R12,000 - R25,000 (belt and oil pump service)

known_faults.description: Pre-facelift automatic EcoSports used Ford's PowerShift dual-clutch gearbox, which is prone to shudder when pulling away and harsh low-speed shifts. Later cars moved to a conventional torque-converter automatic.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Confirm which gearbox the car has. In traffic, check for juddering from standstill and delayed or jerky shifts between first and second.
known_faults.estimated_repair_zar: R10,000 - R30,000 (clutch pack or control module)
known_faults.source: International Ford PowerShift owner reports and class actions

known_faults.fault: Rear spare wheel carrier and tailgate corrosion
known_faults.description: The tailgate-mounted spare wheel carrier and its hinges can corrode, particularly on coastal cars.
known_faults.what_to_inspect: Remove the spare wheel cover and inspect the carrier, hinges and tailgate edges for rust. Check the side-hinged tailgate opens and closes cleanly.

what_to_inspect_before_buying: On 1.0 EcoBoost cars, check coolant level when cold and look for leaks or white residue
Demand full service history with correct-spec oil, critical for the wet timing belt
Run a VIN check for completed Ford recall work
Watch the temperature gauge during a 20-minute test drive
Identify the automatic gearbox type and test for judder in stop-start traffic
Inspect the rear spare wheel carrier and tailgate hinges for rust
Consider the 1.5 petrol as the lower-risk choice for high-mileage cars
owner_sentiment: Mixed. Owners like the high driving position, compact size for city parking and good ground clearance for gravel roads, and the 1.0 EcoBoost is punchy and economical when healthy. Complaints centre on EcoBoost cooling problems, the cramped boot, the side-hinged tailgate in tight parking, and fast depreciation since Ford stopped selling it.
